meta.title: Karol ‘Taidi’ Tajduś — AI beyond the proof of concept
meta.description: Keynotes and workshops about deploying AI in large organizations. No magic tricks. Accountability for outcomes.

hero.title: AI ambition often grows faster
hero.accent: than a company’s ability to deliver on it.
hero.lead: I help executives understand why promising proofs of concept never become real change — and what it takes to make them work.

truthsIntro.eyebrow: From the boardroom and the delivery front line
truthsIntro.title: Five truths about why AI proofs of concept die
truthsIntro.lead: The model usually works in the demo. The real problem comes next: someone has to own it, integrate it into the process and convince people to actually use it.

truths.title: The POC has no problem owner
truths.body: The technology team delivers, but nobody in the business has the mandate, budget or personal accountability to implement it.

truths.title: A demo pretends to be a product
truths.body: A working prototype is only a hypothesis. Scaling begins when integration, security, process and users enter the room.

truths.title: We measure excitement, not change
truths.body: Applause after a presentation cannot tell you whether a solution shortened a process, reduced risk or changed human decisions.

truths.title: AI gets an exemption from the rules
truths.body: The experiment bypasses architecture and compliance, then discovers there is no path to production. Governance should accelerate, not obstruct.

truths.title: The organization is not ready to change
truths.body: Even the best model cannot implement itself. Without new roles, habits and decisions, AI remains a presentation about the future.

about.title: I connect the perspectives of a technologist, advisor and enterprise leader.
paragraphs: I have worked with technology, data and AI for 15 years. My professional thesis is simple: AI projects in large companies do not die for lack of a model. They die between demo and production — on knowledge, integration and governance. Everything I do is about closing that gap.

During 12 years at Accenture, I built a Data & AI team from scratch and grew it beyond 70 people with dozens of deployments. I led global technology programs involving more than 350 specialists and budgets above USD 80 million. Altogether, I have delivered more than 50 technology and Data & AI projects.
Today I lead the AI transformation at Bank Pekao. Around 95% of our AI implementations are built internally, keeping the architecture, development and accountability within the bank.

I lecture on postgraduate AI transformation programs and train executives to deploy AI in regulated organizations. I also speak publicly about moving beyond the proof of concept, including in PFR’s ‘Start with Polish AI’ series.

work.title: The scale where AI has to work for real

items.title: Building Data & AI at Accenture
items.body: From zero to more than 70 people and dozens of deployments. This was not a recruitment exercise, but the creation of capabilities and services that had not previously existed in the firm.

items.title: Global technology programs
items.body: More than 350 specialists, budgets above USD 80 million and international clients. At this scale, a governance error costs more than an error in code.

items.title: AI transformation at Bank Pekao
items.body: An operating model built from the ground up: Responsible AI, hybrid architecture and a working portfolio spanning GenAI for employees and customers, agents, Contact Center and AI-assisted software development.
